sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor's satisfies the accredited US degree route if completed by entry; university minimum
undergraduate GPA 2.75. Mathematics expects substantial proof-based algebra and analysis. International
applicants are eligible; current F-1 does not turn this into a domestic application. [s1] [s5]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD, rather than the separate Applied Mathematics program. Assemble transcripts, CV,
personal statement and referees; request the study-based English exemption with official records. No prior
faculty agreement is published as a prerequisite. Funding/visa evidence is requested after admission. [s1] [s4]
[s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance adviser commitment required publicly. Research-fit contacts below are active faculty in the
requested areas; ask about Fall 2027 supervision. Admissions logistics go to gradmath@colorado.edu.
Geometry beyond the listed algebraic geometers is primarily differential/noncommutative, so not automatically
complex-algebraic fit. [s1] [s10] [s12] [s13] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application; public help documents early referee invitations, status tracking and payment. Do not submit
until CV/statement uploads are final. International financial proof follows admission; no invitation or application
has been sent during research. [s4] [s5]
Cycle verification [Unresolved]
Standing Mathematics deadlines/test policies verified, but explicit Fall 2027 application year and 2027 stipend
not published on inspected pages. Central English table uses the 2026 TOEFL scale; funding amount is
explicitly AY 2026-27 with a typographical problem. [s1] [s2] [s6] [s9]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Current central mathematics table: TOEFL iBT26 5.0, earlier iBT 100, IELTS 7.5, Duolingo 135, Pearson 75 or
Cambridge 190. Scores must remain within two years of admission. Department's older page gives IELTS 7.0,
so follow the higher current table pending written confirmation. Verifiable reports can be uploaded/emailed;
agency reports may be required if unverifiable. [s1] [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Study exemption requires at least one completed full-time academic year at a US/qualifying-country university,
studies ending within two years before intended entry, and official transcript proof. Thus recent UChicago study
should qualify if these conditions hold; it is not citizenship-based. Medium-of-instruction letters alone are not
accepted. No separate mathematics TA oral-testing exemption verified. [s6]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not accepted by Mathematics. [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional but strongly recommended; department says a score above 550 strengthens an application. Unofficial
scores accepted initially. No score-free neutrality claim: omission is permitted but the recommendation is
explicit. [s2]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
Department publishes only the older AY 2024-25 TA stipend of US$27,369 for a 50% appointment; this is not a
2027 offer. Central AY 2026-27 page prints '$14.001 per semester', an apparent punctuation error that must be
confirmed, so no corrected annual total is asserted. Current ≥20% appointments cover mandatory fees,
approximately 90% of student health premiums and dental insurance; vision costs extra. Department's older
fee-exclusion statement conflicts. Tuition remission applies, with approval needed above 15 credits. [s1] [s7] [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Support is renewed subject to departmental standards; no unconditional six-year guarantee located.
Department rules expect completion in six years, permit a seventh funding year only by petition, and do not
promise that extension. Summer teaching/research is often available but not a guaranteed annual salary
component. [s2] [s7] [s8]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students can receive departmental assistantships and nominated fellowships. Department states
their tuition waiver can continue without the Colorado-residency requirement imposed on domestic students.
Confirm every fellowship's citizenship restrictions individually. [s7] [s27]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Ordinary TA appointment is 50%/20 hours weekly including preparation and grading. Mathematics requires
GPA 3.30 after first semester and 3.50 subsequently; central 3.0 is only a minimum. Maintain full-time status,
academic progress and preliminary/comprehensive exam milestones; teacher training is required. Rules
specify two Math 5905 semesters, whereas the support page describes only the first semester. [s7] [s8] [s9]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No public separate incoming TA application established. Ask graduate administration whether the application
contains a funding-interest question. Later summer research and travel support require internal requests,
sometimes adviser endorsement. [s1] [s7]
Other funding routes [Conflict]
First-year summer research groups; later summer teaching if positions exist; after the comprehensive exam,
competitive Thron/Stribic and university research fellowships with adviser support and restrictions on other
employment. Travel assistance is available but old departmental sources disagree on domestic limits ($300
versus $400); international figure $500. None is an admission guarantee. [s2] [s7] [s8]

Application fee [Standing rule]
US$80 international application fee (US$60 domestic); F-1 UChicago attendance does not establish the
domestic category. Pay before the application deadline. [s5] [s26]
Fee waiver [Conflict]
Central program-based waivers generally require US citizenship/permanent residency; ordinary international
applicants are not eligible. A department may fund a waiver, so ask before paying. Public information does not
establish a mathematics hardship waiver for John. Central FAQ allows 14 days for initiated payments, whereas
portal help describes 2-3 days: do not rely on either as a submission extension. [s3] [s4]

Pay attention to
• International deadline is two weeks earlier than domestic; current US F-1 study does not remove it.
• Main essay explicitly asks about teaching and departmental community.
• Do not use the separate Applied Mathematics program's GRE or essay rules.
• Exact 2027 stipend is not verified; older Math funding pages contain several superseded benefit details.
• Faculty shortlist covers direct research matches, excluding emeriti and temporary postdocs. Availability to
take a new student is unconfirmed.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor's satisfies the accredited US degree route if completed by entry; university minimum
undergraduate GPA 2.75. Mathematics expects substantial proof-based algebra and analysis. International
applicants are eligible; current F-1 does not turn this into a domestic application. [s1] [s5]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD, rather than the separate Applied Mathematics program. Assemble transcripts, CV,
personal statement and referees; request the study-based English exemption with official records. No prior
faculty agreement is published as a prerequisite. Funding/visa evidence is requested after admission. [s1] [s4]
[s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance adviser commitment required publicly. Research-fit contacts below are active faculty in the
requested areas; ask about Fall 2027 supervision. Admissions logistics go to gradmath@colorado.edu.
Geometry beyond the listed algebraic geometers is primarily differential/noncommutative, so not automatically
complex-algebraic fit. [s1] [s10] [s12] [s13] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application; public help documents early referee invitations, status tracking and payment. Do not submit
until CV/statement uploads are final. International financial proof follows admission; no invitation or application
has been sent during research. [s4] [s5]
Cycle verification [Unresolved]
Standing Mathematics deadlines/test policies verified, but explicit Fall 2027 application year and 2027 stipend
not published on inspected pages. Central English table uses the 2026 TOEFL scale; funding amount is
explicitly AY 2026-27 with a typographical problem. [s1] [s2] [s6] [s9]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Standing rule]
Standing deadline: December 1 for international applicants (December 15 domestic), 10 p.m. Mountain
Standard Time under the university FAQ. Department and central directory agree. No explicit Fall 2027 year
appears on the inspected mathematics page; verify the portal's dated deadline. John should plan around
December 1, not December 15. [s2] [s3] [s10]

Reference receipt [Standing rule]
Central help permits letters received within 14 days after the program deadline; emailed letters use their sent
date. Applied to the standing December 1 international deadline, December 15 is the derived last letter date;
obtain 2027 confirmation rather than assuming a year-specific extension. [s4]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Central help requires scores by the application deadline. Mathematics accepts self-reported unofficial Math
GRE scores initially. If English exemption is not approved, proof is needed before review; no
mathematics-specific late-score guarantee found. [s2] [s4] [s6]
Supporting documents [Unresolved]
Department allows extra time for supporting materials without publishing a universal end date; only letters
have a verified 14-day rule. Submit applicant-created materials with the application. Official transcripts follow
acceptance; exact incoming 2027 final-record cutoff was not located. [s2] [s4] [s5]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No mathematics-specific or university-wide 2027 acceptance date verified. Other CU departments' April 15
statements do not establish this program's rule. Read the actual academic/funding offers and any deposit
conditions. [s1] [s3]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Current central mathematics table: TOEFL iBT26 5.0, earlier iBT 100, IELTS 7.5, Duolingo 135, Pearson 75 or
Cambridge 190. Scores must remain within two years of admission. Department's older page gives IELTS 7.0,
so follow the higher current table pending written confirmation. Verifiable reports can be uploaded/emailed;
agency reports may be required if unverifiable. [s1] [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Study exemption requires at least one completed full-time academic year at a US/qualifying-country university,
studies ending within two years before intended entry, and official transcript proof. Thus recent UChicago study
should qualify if these conditions hold; it is not citizenship-based. Medium-of-instruction letters alone are not
accepted. No separate mathematics TA oral-testing exemption verified. [s6]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not accepted by Mathematics. [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional but strongly recommended; department says a score above 550 strengthens an application. Unofficial
scores accepted initially. No score-free neutrality claim: omission is permitted but the recommendation is
explicit. [s2]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload unofficial transcripts for every college/university attended, including community-college and summer
coursework; list current study. Original-language records need literal certified English translations.
Study-abroad records may be unnecessary only when complete course/grade/credit/GPA information appears
on the home transcript. Official records follow acceptance, except official proof is specified for the English
exemption. [s3] [s5] [s6] [s11]

Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three recommendations; maximum four. [s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]

Invitation sends when 'send to recommender' is pressed, not merely when details are typed. [s3] [s4]

No: the send button can invite before final application submission; reminders are available afterward. [s3] [s4]

Online letters generate applicant receipt emails and can be monitored on the status page; emailed/Interfolio

Before receipt, exclude and re-add to correct/replace a referee. Confidential Interfolio letters are accepted.
Submitted-letter replacement and cross-cycle reuse are not established. [s4]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV/resume upload required centrally; relevant employment and publications can be included. No public page
limit, prescribed template or font rule found. Applicant-created files cannot be changed after final submission.
[s4]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
The department calls its main essay the personal statement. Faithful paraphrase of requested content:
academic/career goals; mathematical interests and CU fit; alignment with faculty research; teaching
commitment; perspectives on climate, diversity, leadership and teamwork. No public word/page limit or
typography rule found; upload .doc or .pdf. [s1] [s5]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Use the single main personal statement described above. No additional stand-alone background/diversity
essay verified; the main prompt itself includes community and diversity considerations. [s1]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Required as part of the main personal statement; separate research-interest essay not publicly requested. No
independent length/format rule established. [s1]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]

proposal, thesis, paper or writing sample, and any file/length limits, is unverified. The generic portal's mention

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
Department publishes only the older AY 2024-25 TA stipend of US$27,369 for a 50% appointment; this is not a
2027 offer. Central AY 2026-27 page prints '$14.001 per semester', an apparent punctuation error that must be
confirmed, so no corrected annual total is asserted. Current ≥20% appointments cover mandatory fees,
approximately 90% of student health premiums and dental insurance; vision costs extra. Department's older
fee-exclusion statement conflicts. Tuition remission applies, with approval needed above 15 credits. [s1] [s7] [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Support is renewed subject to departmental standards; no unconditional six-year guarantee located.
Department rules expect completion in six years, permit a seventh funding year only by petition, and do not
promise that extension. Summer teaching/research is often available but not a guaranteed annual salary
component. [s2] [s7] [s8]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students can receive departmental assistantships and nominated fellowships. Department states
their tuition waiver can continue without the Colorado-residency requirement imposed on domestic students.
Confirm every fellowship's citizenship restrictions individually. [s7] [s27]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Ordinary TA appointment is 50%/20 hours weekly including preparation and grading. Mathematics requires
GPA 3.30 after first semester and 3.50 subsequently; central 3.0 is only a minimum. Maintain full-time status,
academic progress and preliminary/comprehensive exam milestones; teacher training is required. Rules
specify two Math 5905 semesters, whereas the support page describes only the first semester. [s7] [s8] [s9]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No public separate incoming TA application established. Ask graduate administration whether the application
contains a funding-interest question. Later summer research and travel support require internal requests,
sometimes adviser endorsement. [s1] [s7]
Other funding routes [Conflict]
First-year summer research groups; later summer teaching if positions exist; after the comprehensive exam,
competitive Thron/Stribic and university research fellowships with adviser support and restrictions on other
employment. Travel assistance is available but old departmental sources disagree on domestic limits ($300
versus $400); international figure $500. None is an admission guarantee. [s2] [s7] [s8]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor's satisfies the accredited US degree route if completed by entry; university minimum
undergraduate GPA 2.75. Mathematics expects substantial proof-based algebra and analysis. International
applicants are eligible; current F-1 does not turn this into a domestic application. [s1] [s5]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select Mathematics PhD, rather than the separate Applied Mathematics program. Assemble transcripts, CV,
personal statement and referees; request the study-based English exemption with official records. No prior
faculty agreement is published as a prerequisite. Funding/visa evidence is requested after admission. [s1] [s4]
[s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance adviser commitment required publicly. Research-fit contacts below are active faculty in the
requested areas; ask about Fall 2027 supervision. Admissions logistics go to gradmath@colorado.edu.
Geometry beyond the listed algebraic geometers is primarily differential/noncommutative, so not automatically
complex-algebraic fit. [s1] [s10] [s12] [s13] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application; public help documents early referee invitations, status tracking and payment. Do not submit
until CV/statement uploads are final. International financial proof follows admission; no invitation or application
has been sent during research. [s4] [s5]
Cycle verification [Unresolved]
Standing Mathematics deadlines/test policies verified, but explicit Fall 2027 application year and 2027 stipend
not published on inspected pages. Central English table uses the 2026 TOEFL scale; funding amount is
explicitly AY 2026-27 with a typographical problem. [s1] [s2] [s6] [s9]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Standing rule]
Standing deadline: December 1 for international applicants (December 15 domestic), 10 p.m. Mountain
Standard Time under the university FAQ. Department and central directory agree. No explicit Fall 2027 year
appears on the inspected mathematics page; verify the portal's dated deadline. John should plan around
December 1, not December 15. [s2] [s3] [s10]

Funding consideration [Unresolved]
No separate incoming mathematics assistantship deadline found; apply by the international application
deadline for consideration. Exact Fall 2027 scholarship nomination schedules and any extra funding form
remain unverified. [s1] [s7] [s27]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
Central help permits letters received within 14 days after the program deadline; emailed letters use their sent
date. Applied to the standing December 1 international deadline, December 15 is the derived last letter date;
obtain 2027 confirmation rather than assuming a year-specific extension. [s4]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Central help requires scores by the application deadline. Mathematics accepts self-reported unofficial Math
GRE scores initially. If English exemption is not approved, proof is needed before review; no
mathematics-specific late-score guarantee found. [s2] [s4] [s6]
Supporting documents [Unresolved]
Department allows extra time for supporting materials without publishing a universal end date; only letters
have a verified 14-day rule. Submit applicant-created materials with the application. Official transcripts follow
acceptance; exact incoming 2027 final-record cutoff was not located. [s2] [s4] [s5]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No mathematics-specific or university-wide 2027 acceptance date verified. Other CU departments' April 15
statements do not establish this program's rule. Read the actual academic/funding offers and any deposit
conditions. [s1] [s3]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Current central mathematics table: TOEFL iBT26 5.0, earlier iBT 100, IELTS 7.5, Duolingo 135, Pearson 75 or
Cambridge 190. Scores must remain within two years of admission. Department's older page gives IELTS 7.0,
so follow the higher current table pending written confirmation. Verifiable reports can be uploaded/emailed;
agency reports may be required if unverifiable. [s1] [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Study exemption requires at least one completed full-time academic year at a US/qualifying-country university,
studies ending within two years before intended entry, and official transcript proof. Thus recent UChicago study
should qualify if these conditions hold; it is not citizenship-based. Medium-of-instruction letters alone are not
accepted. No separate mathematics TA oral-testing exemption verified. [s6]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not accepted by Mathematics. [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional but strongly recommended; department says a score above 550 strengthens an application. Unofficial
scores accepted initially. No score-free neutrality claim: omission is permitted but the recommendation is
explicit. [s2]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload unofficial transcripts for every college/university attended, including community-college and summer
coursework; list current study. Original-language records need literal certified English translations.
Study-abroad records may be unnecessary only when complete course/grade/credit/GPA information appears
on the home transcript. Official records follow acceptance, except official proof is specified for the English
exemption. [s3] [s5] [s6] [s11]

Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics-course inventory, textbook list or course-description attachment is requested in the
inspected public admissions instructions. Portal-specific additions and their format/limits remain unverified; do
not assume unsolicited uploads are permitted. [s1] [s5]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three recommendations; maximum four. [s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No extra incoming mathematics scholarship reference or distinct scholarship questionnaire found. Later
departmental summer research fellowships use an adviser recommendation; this is separate from admission.
[s7]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Invitation sends when 'send to recommender' is pressed, not merely when details are typed. [s3] [s4]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
No: the send button can invite before final application submission; reminders are available afterward. [s3] [s4]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Online letters generate applicant receipt emails and can be monitored on the status page; emailed/Interfolio
letters do not generate that email. [s3] [s4]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Before receipt, exclude and re-add to correct/replace a referee. Confidential Interfolio letters are accepted.
Submitted-letter replacement and cross-cycle reuse are not established. [s4]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV/resume upload required centrally; relevant employment and publications can be included. No public page
limit, prescribed template or font rule found. Applicant-created files cannot be changed after final submission.
[s4]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
The department calls its main essay the personal statement. Faithful paraphrase of requested content:
academic/career goals; mathematical interests and CU fit; alignment with faculty research; teaching
commitment; perspectives on climate, diversity, leadership and teamwork. No public word/page limit or
typography rule found; upload .doc or .pdf. [s1] [s5]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Use the single main personal statement described above. No additional stand-alone background/diversity
essay verified; the main prompt itself includes community and diversity considerations. [s1]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Required as part of the main personal statement; separate research-interest essay not publicly requested. No
independent length/format rule established. [s1]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
Not listed as a required mathematics admission document. Whether the program portal accepts an optional
proposal, thesis, paper or writing sample, and any file/length limits, is unverified. The generic portal's mention
of writing samples is not proof Mathematics requests one. [s1] [s4]

Publications list [Unresolved]
Publications may be listed on the CV before submission, including work under review. No separate
publication-list requirement or permission to upload/link full papers verified. [s4]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics-course inventory, textbook list or course-description attachment is requested in the
inspected public admissions instructions. Portal-specific additions and their format/limits remain unverified; do
not assume unsolicited uploads are permitted. [s1] [s5]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
No separate incoming mathematics scholarship essay identified in the public admissions/funding instructions.
Obtain named fellowship requirements before drafting; later internal awards have their own processes. [s7]

Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
No other mathematics-specific written prompt verified. Inspect the live program-specific questions before final
submission because applicant-created materials cannot subsequently be revised. [s4] [s5]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
Department publishes only the older AY 2024-25 TA stipend of US$27,369 for a 50% appointment; this is not a
2027 offer. Central AY 2026-27 page prints '$14.001 per semester', an apparent punctuation error that must be
confirmed, so no corrected annual total is asserted. Current ≥20% appointments cover mandatory fees,
approximately 90% of student health premiums and dental insurance; vision costs extra. Department's older
fee-exclusion statement conflicts. Tuition remission applies, with approval needed above 15 credits. [s1] [s7] [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Support is renewed subject to departmental standards; no unconditional six-year guarantee located.
Department rules expect completion in six years, permit a seventh funding year only by petition, and do not
promise that extension. Summer teaching/research is often available but not a guaranteed annual salary
component. [s2] [s7] [s8]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students can receive departmental assistantships and nominated fellowships. Department states
their tuition waiver can continue without the Colorado-residency requirement imposed on domestic students.
Confirm every fellowship's citizenship restrictions individually. [s7] [s27]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Ordinary TA appointment is 50%/20 hours weekly including preparation and grading. Mathematics requires
GPA 3.30 after first semester and 3.50 subsequently; central 3.0 is only a minimum. Maintain full-time status,
academic progress and preliminary/comprehensive exam milestones; teacher training is required. Rules
specify two Math 5905 semesters, whereas the support page describes only the first semester. [s7] [s8] [s9]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No public separate incoming TA application established. Ask graduate administration whether the application
contains a funding-interest question. Later summer research and travel support require internal requests,
sometimes adviser endorsement. [s1] [s7]
Other funding routes [Conflict]
First-year summer research groups; later summer teaching if positions exist; after the comprehensive exam,
competitive Thron/Stribic and university research fellowships with adviser support and restrictions on other
employment. Travel assistance is available but old departmental sources disagree on domestic limits ($300
versus $400); international figure $500. None is an admission guarantee. [s2] [s7] [s8]

Application fee [Standing rule]
US$80 international application fee (US$60 domestic); F-1 UChicago attendance does not establish the
domestic category. Pay before the application deadline. [s5] [s26]
Fee waiver [Conflict]
Central program-based waivers generally require US citizenship/permanent residency; ordinary international
applicants are not eligible. A department may fund a waiver, so ask before paying. Public information does not
establish a mathematics hardship waiver for John. Central FAQ allows 14 days for initiated payments, whereas
portal help describes 2-3 days: do not rely on either as a submission extension. [s3] [s4]

Department IELTS 7 versus central Math 7.5; older department student-fee liability versus current central

punctuation '$14.001'. Do not substitute Applied Mathematics rules. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s6] [s7] [s8] [s9]
